questions.question: Describe three methods used by abolitionists in the United States and name three leading abolitionists.
questions.expected_answer: Methods: newspapers (The Liberator), pamphlets, books (Uncle Tom's Cabin) and lectures; petitions to Congress; testimony of formerly enslaved people; boycotts; helping escapers via the Underground Railroad. Abolitionists: Frederick Douglass, William Lloyd Garrison, Sojourner Truth, the Grimke sisters, Harriet Tubman, Harriet Beecher Stowe.

questions.question: Describe John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry: its aims, events and outcome.
questions.expected_answer: Aim: seize weapons from the federal armoury, arm enslaved people and start an uprising from a base in the mountains. On 16 October 1859 Brown led 21 men (16 white, 5 Black) and captured the armoury and hostages, but few enslaved people joined; militia surrounded the town; on 18 October Marines under Robert E. Lee stormed the engine house, killing ten raiders including two of Brown's sons and capturing Brown, who was tried for treason and murder and hanged on 2 December 1859.

questions.question: Explain why John Brown is viewed differently by different groups, and outline how slavery was finally abolished in the United States.
questions.expected_answer: White Southerners saw him as a murderer, terrorist and fanatic who confirmed fears of Northern aggression; many abolitionists and Black Americans saw him as a martyr who gave his life for the enslaved and treated Black people as equals; historians weigh his moral courage against his violence, such as the Pottawatomie killings. Lincoln's election in 1860 led Southern states to secede; the Civil War (1861-1865) followed; the 1863 Emancipation Proclamation freed enslaved people in Confederate states and about 180 000 Black soldiers fought for the Union; the Thirteenth Amendment of 1865 abolished slavery, freeing about four million people.
